title: Rabbi David Tawil: Shemuel II Chapter 11- "David & BatSheva"

chapters.title: Introduction to Shemuel Bet Chapter 11
chapters.about: Context of David's kingdom and the challenge of the narrative

chapters.title: David and Bat-Sheva
chapters.about: The text of the encounter and the initial analysis of the events

chapters.title: Culpability and Coercion
chapters.about: Discussion on Bat-Sheva's role and the Gemara in Masekhet Ketubot

chapters.title: The Vantage Point of the Roof
chapters.about: Radak's explanation of the scene and the issue of modesty

chapters.title: Uriah's Return
chapters.about: David's attempt to manipulate Uriah and Uriah's refusal

summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the challenging narrative of David HaMelech and Bat-Sheva in Shemuel Bet, chapter 11. He analyzes the text to understand David's actions, the role of Uriah HaChiti, and the perspectives of the Hakhamim regarding culpability and coercion in this difficult story.
questions: Why did David remain in Yerushalayim while his army was at war?
How do the Hakhamim address the question of Bat-Sheva's culpability?
What is the significance of the phrase 'bathe your feet' in the text?
Why did Uriah refuse to go home to his wife?
How does the text indicate that David was attempting to cover his tracks?
